article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 80% indica / 20% sativa
Genetics: OG Kush × BF Super Auto #1
Breeder: Barney’s Farm
THC Content: 20–24%
CBD Content: N/A
Terpene Profile: Myrcene , limonene , and caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Sour citrus, woody pine, dank Kush
Flowering Time (Indoor): 70–75 days from seed to harvest
Outdoor Harvest Time: 70–75 days from germination
Indoor Yield: 450–550 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 180–250 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

OG Kush has spent decades influencing West Coast marijuana breeding , but the traditional photoperiod plant requires a seasonal or artificial change in light to begin flowering. OG Kush Auto takes that familiar Kush personality and compresses it into a much faster cultivation schedule. Barney’s Farm accomplished this by combining its OG Kush genetics with BF Super Auto #1, producing a compact automatic plant that retains the earthy, pine-heavy, lemon-fuel character associated with the family while reaching harvest in roughly ten to eleven weeks from germination.

The finished cannabis favors physical relaxation over energetic stimulation, yet its opening phase can carry enough euphoria and mental lift to keep the experience from becoming immediately sleepy. For growers, the attraction is equally straightforward: substantial yields, manageable height, automatic flowering, and recognizable Kush aroma without waiting for autumn or manipulating a 12/12 indoor light cycle.
Genetics and Lineage

The breeder identifies the cross precisely as OG Kush × BF Super Auto #1. That first parent carries the famous West Coast Kush profile, while the second supplies the autoflowering trait necessary for plants to begin blooming according to age instead of changing daylight duration. Barney’s Farm describes its photoperiod OG Kush as descending from Chemdawg , Lemon Thai , and Hindu Kush , a combination that helps explain the cultivar’s mixture of pungent fuel, citrus, earth, and deep Kush character. The company’s photoperiod OG Kush is 70% indica, whereas this automatic version moves slightly further toward the indica side at 80%.

Introducing automatic genetics changes the plant’s life cycle more dramatically than its basic personality. Autoflowers transition into bloom based primarily on maturity rather than photoperiod, allowing outdoor gardeners to complete crops without waiting for progressively shorter days late in the season. Barney’s Farm reports 70–75 days from seed for this particular line. That distinction also means OG Kush Auto should not be treated as genetically interchangeable with similarly named automatic Kush cultivars from other seed companies. Breeders use different OG selections and different autoflowering parents, so potency, structure, harvest time, and flavor can vary considerably even when the package carries a nearly identical strain name.
Effects and Experience

The experience begins with more brightness than an 80% indica classification might imply. Barney’s Farm describes euphoric, cerebral, happy, sociable, and uplifting qualities alongside the cultivar’s stronger relaxing tendencies. A moderate serving can create an initial improvement in mood and a softer mental atmosphere before the body becomes increasingly prominent. Conversation may remain appealing during the first phase, and familiar music or low-key entertainment can feel more absorbing without producing the restless stimulation associated with some strongly sativa-leaning weed .

As the session develops, the Kush side takes control. Physical tension can give way to a heavier body sensation, activity becomes less compelling, and larger doses may make a sofa considerably more attractive than a busy schedule. With breeder-listed THC reaching 24%, inexperienced consumers should approach gradually rather than assuming an autoflower is automatically mild. THC affects judgment, coordination, perception, and reaction time, and the CDC advises that cannabis impairs skills necessary for safe driving. This cultivar therefore fits much better into an evening at home than before driving, work requiring precision, or other safety-sensitive responsibilities.
Medical Benefits

The combination of euphoria and substantial physical relaxation helps explain why Kush-family cannabis remains popular among some medical marijuana consumers. Barney’s Farm associates its OG Kush Auto with calming effects and specifically discusses its use by consumers seeking relief associated with pain, anxiety, and sleeplessness. Those descriptions should not be interpreted as clinical proof that this particular strain treats those disorders. Cannabis sold under a strain name is not a standardized pharmaceutical preparation, and cannabinoid concentrations can vary according to phenotype, cultivation practices, harvest maturity, storage, and laboratory testing.

For patients who already tolerate THC, the cultivar’s heavier evening character may be preferable when daytime alertness is no longer important. Others may find a high-THC product counterproductive. NIDA notes that THC-containing cannabis can change mood, thoughts, and perception, and some individuals experience anxiety or other unwanted psychological effects. Anyone using weed alongside prescription medication, managing significant psychiatric symptoms, or attempting to control persistent pain or sleep problems should discuss cannabis use with a qualified healthcare professional rather than relying solely on weed strain descriptions .
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Classic Kush character is the center of the aromatic profile. Barney’s Farm lists sour citrus, woody pine, and dank Kush as the primary flavors, while the aroma expands into earth, pungent skunk, lemon citrus, sourness, and lemon-fuel. Opening a well-cured flower should therefore produce a sharper experience than the sugary dessert profiles found throughout modern cannabis breeding. Lemon peel and pine arrive near the top, while damp soil, hash-like Kush, skunk, and gasoline-like pungency provide the darker foundation.

Barney’s Farm does not publish individual laboratory terpene percentages for the Auto release, so assigning it a fixed chemical hierarchy would be misleading. Its photoperiod OG Kush parent, however, is described by the breeder as carrying myrcene, limonene, and caryophyllene. Myrcene complements earthy and musky tones, limonene contributes citrus brightness, and caryophyllene introduces peppery spice. The automatic offspring clearly preserves the parent’s lemon-earth-pine direction based on the breeder’s sensory profile, but the exact terpene balance should be determined from laboratory analysis of the specific harvested batch.
Growing Information

OG Kush Auto is engineered around efficiency. Plants generally remain between 90 and 110 cm indoors, making the cultivar much easier to accommodate than a large photoperiod Kush grown through an extended vegetative period. Outdoor specimens can reach 100–120 cm. Barney’s Farm lists indoor yields of 450–550 g/m² and 180–250 g from an individual outdoor plant, impressive numbers for cannabis that completes its entire life cycle in only 70–75 days. Because blooming occurs automatically, an outdoor gardener can potentially schedule harvest according to germination date rather than waiting for a particular week in September or October.

The plant combines relatively compact dimensions with enough branching to develop a productive canopy. Indoor gardeners can use gentle low-stress training to spread growth horizontally and expose additional flower sites, but severe stress early in life is usually less forgiving with autos because their vegetative clock cannot simply be extended for another several weeks. Healthy root development, consistent irrigation, stable lighting, and gradual feeding are more valuable than aggressive manipulation. Dense Kush flowers also benefit from reliable airflow as they increase in mass late in bloom.

Strong aroma is another practical consideration. The breeder describes the plant as pungent, skunky, earthy, and fuel-heavy, meaning indoor gardens may become conspicuous well before harvest. A well-maintained growing environment should provide sufficient air exchange while avoiding excessive humidity around dense flowers. Overall, its manageable dimensions, automatic schedule, and strong production potential make it accessible to newer growers, while experienced cultivators can use careful canopy management to push yields toward the upper end of the breeder’s range.
FAQ
Is OG Kush Auto indica or sativa?

Barney’s Farm classifies its OG Kush Auto as 80% indica and 20% sativa. The effects reflect that composition, beginning with some cerebral uplift before becoming increasingly relaxing and body-focused.
What are the genetics of OG Kush Auto?
The official Barney’s Farm cross is OG Kush × BF Super Auto #1. The OG Kush parent itself is listed by the breeder as descending from Chemdawg, Lemon Thai, and Hindu Kush genetics.
How strong is OG Kush Auto?

Barney’s Farm currently lists THC at 24%, while its longer cultivar description gives a range of approximately 20–24%. Actual harvested cannabis may test differently depending on phenotype and cultivation conditions.
How long does OG Kush Auto take to grow?

The complete cycle takes approximately 70–75 days from seed under suitable conditions. Since the plant flowers automatically, there is no need to switch indoor lighting to 12 hours of darkness to trigger bloom.
How much does OG Kush Auto yield?

Indoor gardens can produce approximately 450–550 g/m², while outdoor plants are rated at roughly 180–250 g each. Light intensity, root space, plant health, nutrition, climate, and training all influence whether a crop approaches those figures.
Final Thoughts on OG Kush Auto

OG Kush Auto delivers its strongest argument through familiarity rather than novelty. Barney’s Farm has taken one of marijuana’s most recognizable genetic families and paired it with BF Super Auto #1 to create an 80% indica automatic cultivar that preserves the lemon, pine, earth, skunk, and fuel character expected from Kush genetics. Its effect unfolds in two useful stages: a happier and somewhat sociable cerebral opening followed by increasingly substantial physical relaxation. At up to 24% THC, the result retains enough potency to satisfy experienced consumers despite the abbreviated growing cycle.

Cultivators gain an equally practical combination. A 70–75 day seed-to-harvest schedule, 90–110 cm indoor height, and potential 450–550 g/m² production make the plant suitable for growers who want classic-style weed without committing months to vegetative growth and photoperiod management. It does not replace traditional OG Kush genetically—the autoflower parent necessarily changes the line—but it translates many of that cultivar’s defining qualities into a faster and more manageable form. For anyone seeking old-school Kush flavor, strong evening effects, and the convenience of automatic flowering, OG Kush Auto occupies a well-defined place in the modern autoflower category.
